edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 12

source_text: Similis est fratruelis meus capreae vel hinnulo cervorum super montes domus Dei. Bethel quippe domus Dei interpretatur. Non omnes montes domus Dei sunt; sunt montes superbientes et praerupti, de quibus dicitur: Quare contenditis, montes coagulati? Montes autem Domini prophetae et apostoli sunt. Caprea et hinnulus in his montibus versantur, quia Christus in prophetis et apostolis cognoscitur. Surge, propera, proxima mea, speciosa mea, columba mea. Iam hiems transiit; imber abiit et recessit; flores apparuerunt in terra; tempus putationis advenit; vox turturis audita est in terra nostra. Ficus protulit grossos suos; vineae florentes dederunt odorem. Surge, propera, proxima mea. Quare surge? Quia hiems passionis transiit, quia imber temptationum abiit, quia flores resurrectionis apparuerunt, quia vox Spiritus sancti — turturis — in ecclesia audita est.
pass_a_gloss: Like is my brother to-gazelle or young-of stags upon mountains of-house of-God. Bethel indeed house of-God is-interpreted. Not all mountains house of-God are; there-are mountains being-proud and sheer, about which it-is-said: Why do-you-contend, mountains curdled? Mountains however of-Lord prophets and apostles are. Gazelle and young-stag in these mountains turn-about, because Christ in prophets and apostles is-known. Arise, hasten, my neighbor, my fair, my dove. Already winter passed; rain went-away and withdrew; flowers appeared in land; time of-pruning arrived; voice of-turtledove heard is in land our. Fig put-forth its green-figs; vines flowering gave smell. Arise, hasten, my neighbor. Why arise? Because winter of-passion passed, because rain of-temptations went-away, because flowers of-resurrection appeared, because voice of-Holy Spirit — of-turtledove — in church heard is.
pass_b_english: [[My brother is like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of the house of God >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:9]]. For Bethel is interpreted house of God. Not all mountains are the house of God; there are proud and sheer mountains, of which it is said: [[Why do you contend, you curdled mountains? >> Bible:Psalm 68:16]]. But the mountains of the Lord are the prophets and apostles. The gazelle and young stag move among these mountains, because Christ is known in the prophets and apostles. [[Arise, make haste, my neighbor, my fair one, my dove >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:10]]. [[For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone; the flowers have appeared in the land; the time of pruning has come; the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land. The fig tree has put forth its green figs; the flowering vines have given their fragrance. Arise, make haste, my neighbor >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:11-13]]. Why arise? Because the winter of the passion is past, because the rain of temptations is gone, because the flowers of the resurrection have appeared, because the voice of the Holy Spirit — the turtledove — has been heard in the church.
